cycles.description: Elapsed teaching cycles shared by CPU execution and storage I/O.
cycles.domain: Each gate advances up to 10 cycles; action latency follows the current teaching configuration.
cycles.source: One clock advances independent CPU and serial boot/storage lanes; concurrent durations are not added together.

memory.description: Allocated physical memory and page-file blocks.
memory.domain: 16, 32 or 48 RAM blocks representing 4, 8 or 12 GB.

latency.domain: L1 1, L2 5, L3 14, RAM 45 cycles; storage and page-file transfers are longer.
latency.output: Storage progress, CPU fetch source, latency reference and approximate transfer-time comparison.

modes.configuration: Three RAM sizes, three cache configurations, SSD/HDD, five clock animation speeds.
modes.workload: Boot, open work apps, stress memory and close background apps, plus desktop application interactions.
modes.support: Open simulation without Working, exam toggle or terminal score.

dependencies: Starting the clock loads the OS before workload shortcuts become available.
Storage completion updates RAM/page-file ownership; CPU reference completion updates cache entries and hit metrics.
Configuration changes reset both lanes, blocked threads and handler jobs. Scheduling preserves the learner-selected foreground application.
The first opened desktop application dismisses the shared icon introduction across subsequent redraws.

Core evidence identifies the running thread and sampled cache/RAM reference. Storage-backed faults block the requester; OS handler work queues I/O and completion makes the requester ready to retry the same reference. Edge-anchored paths resize with the devices.

A round-robin CPU stream serves ready applications and periodic OS work. Cache/RAM misses stall that thread; storage transfers continue independently. Demand page-ins precede background launch loads and remain FIFO with each other. Closing an app clears its references and blocked state.
implementation.completion: No terminal gate; learners compare access routes and memory pressure over repeated workloads.
limitations: Relative teaching latencies and approximate hardware comparison are simplified rather than hardware benchmarks.
Desktop process identities remain aligned with allocated block colours.

One CPU core, one serial storage lane, 24-cycle scheduling quanta checked between completed references, 6-cycle application work bursts, 8-cycle OS handlers and periodic OS work every 120 teaching cycles. These are sampled references, not instruction-accurate execution or a production OS scheduler. Cache entries identify referenced pages rather than physical cache lines; RAM-pinned OS pages are not cache-pinned.
